name: Planarity
miniText: How can moving vertices remove visual crossings without changing a graph's connections? NetLogo Planarity generates a solvable graph, scrambles vertex positions, and lets a player drag vertices until no edges cross. Hopcroft and Tarjan [1] establish algorithmic planarity testing, Tutte [2] studies graph drawing, and computational geometry [3] supplies segment-intersection and geometric representation methods. These sources clarify the difference between a graph's abstract topology and one particular drawing. A planar graph may initially look tangled, while some abstract graphs admit no crossing-free embedding. The baseline intentionally supplies solvable instances, so repeated success does not demonstrate a general planarity decision algorithm. Crossing detection depends on finite coordinates and the treatment of shared endpoints. The experiment illustrates geometric reorganization under fixed connectivity rather than a change in the underlying network.
